identity.name: Calcium malates
identity.chemical_class: Calcium salts of malic acid (hydroxy-dicarboxylate salts)

function.mechanism: Provides malate-based acidification/buffering and contributes sourness modulation in formulated foods.

adi.basis: No EFSA numeric ADI for E352 identified from accessible EFSA pages in this session; 2018 EFSA DCM opinion reported insufficient evidence to complete novel-food safety assessment.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA ANS (2018) considered evidence insufficient to distinguish proposed di-calcium malate dossier from already authorised calcium malate sources and could not complete a full safety assessment for that novel-food submission.

fda.cfr_citation: No direct calcium malate listing found in 21 CFR Title 21 full XML (issue date 2026-02-19); related section: 21 CFR 184.1069 (malic acid, GRAS)

adi.basis: ADI not specified (group ADI for DL-malic acid and sodium, potassium and calcium salts).

concerns.summary: A 2025 prospective cohort observed higher type 2 diabetes incidence for certain food additive mixtures that included malic acid among multiple co-exposures; this is mixture-level observational evidence and not calcium-malate-specific causality.
Evidence-quality gap: EFSA 2018 reported insufficient dossier characterization/exposure information for di-calcium malate novel-food evaluation.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA assigned ADI 'not specified' for DL-malic acid and sodium/potassium/calcium salts (1979).
No IARC monograph group classification for calcium malate/malic acid was identified in the checked IARC classification dataset.

adi_exceedance.notes: No numerical ADI was set by JECFA (ADI not specified) and no EFSA numeric ADI for E352 was identified; additive-specific exceedance quantification could not be calculated from accessible sources.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory baseline (JECFA ADI not specified) and lack of direct carcinogenic classification support low-to-limited concern at typical use levels, but evidence quality is constrained by sparse recent additive-specific toxicology and incomplete modern exposure characterization for E352.
key_factors: No IARC classification identified for calcium malate
No direct standalone calcium malate CFR listing found in current Title 21 XML
